S37.01.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one project
S37.01.note: The code calls these projects, not notebooks; the Expected item's notebook is the same object as a project.
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and click the More button (tooltip More).
Click Projects in the menu.
Look for a list of your projects with the placeholder Open a project. If you are signed out, the list shows Sign in to see your projects instead.
Click one project in the list and check that its detail menu opens with the project name as its title.
S37.01.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Projects (or Command Palette > Code: Show Projects)

steps: Click More in the AGI Code sidebar, then click Projects.
Click the New project icon at the top of the list (tooltip New project).
Type a name such as QA test notebook and press Enter. An empty name is refused with the message A project needs a name.
Leave Instructions empty and press Enter, or type some and press Enter.
Look for the message saying the project is on your account, on every client, and check that the project now appears in the list.
S37.02.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Projects > New project (or Command Palette > Code: New Project)

S37.03.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one project
steps: Open Projects from the More menu and click a project.
Click Rename, type a new name, and press Enter.
Open the same project again, click Description, type a description, and press Enter.
Look for the message saying the project was saved to your account, and check that the new name is the menu title and the description shows under it.
S37.03.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Projects > [project name] > Rename or Description

S37.15.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one project
S37.15.note: In the code, the instructions only reach chat turns in a workspace where the project is used in this chat; the prompt text says every chat in the project, on every client, which is set on the server.
steps: Open Projects from the More menu and click a project.
Click Instructions under the Edit heading, type text such as Always answer in bullet points, and press Enter.
Open the project again and check that Instructions now shows Set.
Click Use in this chat on the project, then send a message in this workspace's chat and compare the reply with the instructions.
S37.15.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Projects > [project name] > Instructions

S37.37.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one project
S37.37.note: The Projects group appears only when the start screen has project suggestions; I did not confirm when it shows. The same Use in this chat item is also in the project menu from More > Projects.
steps: Open a new chat in the AGI Code sidebar.
In the Projects group of the start suggestions, click the Use in this chat button on a project row. The project menu opens.
Click Use in this chat in that menu.
Look at the chip above the message box with a folder icon and the project name (labelled Active project), then send a message in the chat.
S37.37.where: AGI Code chat start screen > Projects group > Use in this chat (then Use in this chat in the project menu)
